source.finding_ref: visual-verification.md In-run fix 2 re-verify, Departure A

defect_class: An element whose glyph or colour encodes the result of comparing two data values is judged only on the comparison branch the mockup draws, so its equal and missing-operand branches ship asserting a direction the data does not show.
why_picked: 1. Defect class: a data-comparison indicator (an arrow, a better/worse colour, a status badge) is verified only on the branch the frame draws. 2. No rule covers it: sweep 8 reads "For each value the view computes from an input the operator can edit" and the first full report recorded "derived n/a — no operator-editable input"; no other sweep compares an indicator's claim with the data it reads. 3. It generalises to every delta, KPI or status view; this run shows the class twice — departures A (equal values drawn as an improvement) and B (a missing before drawn as worse) were both in the first full capture, the first verifier missed both, the second found A and missed B, the third found B, and a brief sweeping every branch then came back clean. 4. It states a principle — an indicator is a claim about data, checked on every branch of its comparison — not a rule about arrows.
before:
8. **Every derived value re-derived after its input changes.** For each value the view
      computes from an input the operator can edit — a delta, a total, a conversion, a preview —
      type a new input, capture before and after, recompute the expected value by hand, and
      state both. A value that does not follow its input, or that is absent on one entry path the
      populated path shows (first-time versus returning), is a defect no single capture can
      show.
after:
8. **Every derived value re-derived after its input changes.** For each value the view
      computes from an input the operator can edit — a delta, a total, a conversion, a preview —
      type a new input, capture before and after, recompute the expected value by hand, and
      state both. A value that does not follow its input, or that is absent on one entry path the
      populated path shows (first-time versus returning), is a defect no single capture can
      show.
      The same holds for every element the view picks from a comparison of data values,
      operator-editable or not — an arrow, a better/worse colour, a status badge, a stroke: list its
      comparison's branches (greater, equal, less, each operand absent), reach each one in a capture,
      seeding the data where none reaches it, and state per capture the values compared and whether
      the element's claim is true of them. An element that asserts a direction its values do not show
      is a defect whatever the frame draws.
